newsitem.title: USA: Frisch's responds on baseball team interest.
newsitem.headline: Frisch's responds on baseball team interest.

text.p: Frisch's Restaurants Inc, responding to two board members' suggestion it sell its minority interest in the Cincinnati Reds baseball team, said Thursday it has been studying the value of that investment.
Marge Schott, the Reds' president and chief executive officer whose colorful personality has often gained media attention, owns the largest share of the team.

Seven others, including Big Boy restaurant chain Frisch's and Cincinnati financier Carl Lindner, each own a small share, a Reds spokesman said. The Reds declined to comment on the possible sale of Frisch's interest.

On Wednesday, board members Barry Nussbaum and Jerry Ruyan issued a statement suggesting Frisch's offer to sell its Reds interest to Cincinnati business and civic leaders because it no longer provides any return for Frisch's.
Nussbaum and Ruyan, with their Wolverine Partners investment firm, have bought about 8.7 percent of Frisch's stock since July 1996. They ousted two incumbent board members last fall.

Frisch's said its board will evaluate all options for enhancing shareholder value. In January the board established a committee to study the Reds investment and factors to consider if they dispose of it, Frisch's said.
Frisch's chided Nussbaum and Ruyan in its statement.

"We are astonished that Mr. Nussbaum and Mr. Ruyan, company directors, would take their proposals directly to the media rather than formally present them first to the board or its special committee," Frisch's said.
It called the duo's media statement "a grandstand play... totally inconsistent with all rules of corporate governance."
